chase_cards.name: Touch Generation Change!
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a rule object before it is a collectible object. It was necessary for a temporary parent/child format that literally asked two generations of card backs, and two generations of people, to hand the game across the table.

key_artists.name: Tomokazu Komiya
key_artists.why: Komiya matters because this could have been a dry rules insert. His loose, deliberately deformed visual language makes the parent/child handoff feel alive, awkward, comic, and human, which is exactly the emotional surface of a tag-change rule.

claims.text: The local catalog models New Garura Parent/Child Tournament participation prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing Touch Generation Change! at source index 246.

Bulbapedia says Touch Generation Change! cards were given to participants of the New Garura Parent/Child Tournament in February 2002 because they were necessary for the New Garura Rules version of the TCG used in the tournament.
Bulbapedia says the New Garura Rules required a deck of 30 cards with the old reverse design, 30 cards with the current reverse design, plus the two promotional cards to initiate a partner switch.

Bulbapedia gives Touch Generation Change!'s effect as shuffling each player's hand into the original deck with the same back side as the card, then allowing each partner to draw up to five cards and tag team with their partner.
Bulbapedia credits both the unnumbered promotional and 027/P P Promotional prints of Touch Generation Change! to Tomokazu Komiya.

Bulbapedia says Touch Generation Change! was released simultaneously as one of the Unnumbered Promotional cards and as P Promotional card 027/P, with the P Promotional print including e-Reader Dot Code data.

Bulbapedia describes Tomokazu Komiya as a Pokemon TCG illustrator and Pokemon Tales book artist whose illustration style is known for deformed and loosely colored images, tied to his use of Primitivism.

Bulbapedia's trivia links Touch Generation Change! to a small lineage of mandatory special-rule Trainer cards: Touch Change! for the original Garura Rules and Touch Exchange! for later Tag Battle Rules.

As judged collector texture, Touch Generation Change! matters because it turns rule infrastructure into a collectible: old and new card backs, parent and child players, and a physical card that lets the table change hands.

Agents should preserve New Garura Parent/Child Tournament route, source index 246, Japanese title タッチ世代交代!, Tomokazu Komiya credit, New Garura Rules exclusive-use status, old-back/current-back deck context, unnumbered-vs-027/P print distinction, and non-equivalence with Touch Change! or Touch Exchange! before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Touch Generation Change!: when the rule card is the family handshake
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of those cards that explains the apparatus better than a trophy does. The New Garura format did not just ask a parent and child to sit together; it built the handoff into the deck. Old backs, current backs, two partners, and a card that tells the table when the generation changes. Komiya's art keeps the rule from feeling sterile. The result is a strange little object that says Pokemon was building rituals of play, not just printing monsters.

narrative.human_title: Touch Generation Change!: the card that tells the table to swap hands
narrative.why_it_matters: This card is all apparatus, in the best way. It does not give you a monster; it gives you a moment in the game where the adult and child exchange agency. The text even cares which back design the hand returns to, so the card is literally managing the boundary between eras of Pokémon cards. That makes it a beautiful object for this catalog: a rule, a family format, a Komiya drawing, and a small proof that the TCG was willing to make weird temporary machines for play.
